headline: Short token cues elicit reasoning behavior associated with training data in tested base models
summary: An arXiv preprint reports that prefilling selected response-opening tokens can raise tested base models’ math accuracy toward that of direct-RL counterparts, and controlled data edits can make arbitrary openings act as reasoning cues. The results support a training-association mechanism in the tested models, while leaving the contribution of RL, generalization and cue-conditioned safety unresolved.
